name: com.openugd.lifetime
description: Structured object lifetimes: a composable scope primitive for deterministic cleanup. A Lifetime collects termination actions and nested scopes; terminating its Definition runs them in reverse registration order, so resources are released at a well-defined point rather than whenever the garbage collector runs. Same model as JetBrains Rider Lifetime/LifetimeDefinition.

samples.description: Who holds the Definition versus who holds the Lifetime. Handing out a Lifetime hands out no authority to end it - the same split as CancellationTokenSource and CancellationToken.
Scopes form a tree: terminating a parent cascades to every child, a child that ends first unregisters itself, and clean-up runs LIFO with failures isolated into an AggregateException.
using var scope = lifetime.DefineNested(...) for an operation with a beginning and an end, and the implicit Definition to Lifetime conversion that downgrades the capability at every call boundary.
AddBracket writes acquire and release as one expression, and disposable.With(lifetime) ties an IDisposable to a scope on the line that constructs it.
AsCancellationToken bridges a scope into async/await code, so ending the scope cancels in-flight work and a token from a dead scope is born cancelled instead of hanging forever.
A scope that ends as soon as either of two independent scopes ends - for things whose validity depends on several lifetimes at once, which the parent-child tree cannot express.
The 2.0.0 rule: registering clean-up on an already-terminated scope runs it immediately rather than dropping it silently, which removes a whole class of leaks.
The only sample that needs Unity: binding a scope to a GameObject, a nested scope for OnEnable/OnDisable, and async work cancelled by destruction. The package itself has no engine dependency.
